report:
Reviewed the complete owner_binder claim, all six ordinary implementation associations, and both associated tests (one ordinary, one TODO). The requirements are owner-only parameter minting under a binder, reuse by associated-item/field/body queries, creation only of new item-level parameters, and preservation of owner GenericParam and Self identities.

Implementation inspection: CheckGenerics in cst/generics.rs creates parameters using the owning Symbol and parameter index, registers exactly those handles and returns their slice. Struct and impl sig methods call it at their tracked owner signature boundary and return the resulting binder. Trait sig creates explicit parameters and one implicit Self parameter owned by the trait, then returns Self followed by the explicit parameters. fns.rs open_owner copies that trait binder, deriving the Self type from binder.value.self_param; for impl owners it copies the existing self type and binder. LocalFnSym::sig registers these owner parameters and calls CheckGenerics only for the function's own declaration, concatenating owner and method slices with owner_generic_count. associated::lower_items accepts owner generics and copies those handles into its item-list binder; trait/impl items callers supply sig().iter_symbols(). Struct fields also use sig().iter_symbols(). LocalFnSym::body obtains sig, registers its parameters, and imports its Self/type/environment values, without calling the minting helper.

Captured generic_param.rs confirms parent/kind/name/index identity fields and tracked source span. Captured Binder/BinderExt code copies semantic handles and iterates the existing generic slice; ribs stores Resolution::Param(gp) directly, and captured import_fn_sig copies owner Self and signature types into body storage without constructing GenericParam. These support the ordinary owner-reopening paths. Associated type aliases/constants have no complete signature API yet: captured existing ty.rs TODOs explicitly require those APIs to reopen owner binders and defer their identity-preservation coverage. This report does not invent completed support for those absent operations or equate a symbol-only enumeration with checking such a signature.

Ordinary test trait_and_impl_signatures_share_complete_generic_binders uses actual Rust source defining Bound, PairBound<T>, and an impl for (T,T). Captured with_test_crate setup adds source files, creates a tracked root, parses source and invokes real queries. Visible assertions check two trait parameters (Self and T), eligible trait signature and one predicate; one impl and one impl parameter, eligible impl signature, two tuple elements and equal checked element types. This is meaningful binder-shape and repeated-parameter-use coverage. It does not explicitly compare the trait Self handle with its binder entry, compare an impl element's handle with binder.generics[0], exercise associated functions/fields/bodies, or edit a persistent database. It is therefore not presented as proof of the whole identity contract.

The associated TODO checking_signature_owner_binder explicitly reserves trait/impl/associated-function/field/body identity comparisons across queries and revisions, including separate owner and method scopes. It has no assertions and remains deferred. Completing it requires source-backed consumers exposing the actual parameter handles from each product, persistent database revisions, and assertions that owner handles are reused while item-local handles stay distinct. Missing associated type/constant signature APIs are a prerequisite for those kinds, as documented by the captured implementation TODO. Together the ordinary test's limited assertions and explicit outstanding matrix honestly account for the claim without claiming complete verification.

Commands executed: fresh cargo meta review start with coordinator instructions; source and complete-test inspection; review read captures for checking design, generic identity definitions, binder/ribs/import helpers, test fixture/root construction, and existing missing-API TODOs. No tests or build were run by this reviewer; central suite execution remains separate evidence. No source changes or new suspected defect requiring reproduction. No requested edits; existing deferred implementation and verification are retained explicitly.
